issues.legal_issue: Possession for the enlargement of a female Hindu’s estate includes constructive possession and is not confined to actual physical possession.
material_facts: The widow had acquired her deceased husband’s estate before the succession legislation came into force.
The alleged adopted son was said to be in actual possession, but his possession was permissive under an agreement that left the widow in possession and enjoyment of the estate.
The court considered the possession issue on the assumption that the adoption was invalid.
issues.conclusion: The statutory term “possessed” has a broad meaning that includes actual, constructive, or other possession recognised by law; the widow was in constructive possession through the permissive holder.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, property possessed by a female Hindu is held by her as full owner. The court approved the interpretation in Gostha Behari v. Haridas Samanta that possession may be actual or constructive, or in any form recognised by law. It also referred to Gaddam Venkayamma v. Gaddam Veerayya, while stating that it need not adopt the full extent of that decision. An appellate court may take account of a change in law, as held in Lachmeshwar Prasad Shukul v. Keshwar Lal Chaudhuri.

predicates.female_estate_enlargement_claim: A claim concerns whether a female Hindu’s property interest is enlarged under a rule that applies to property she possesses.
predicates.female_hindu_has_property: A female Hindu has a property interest in the property at issue.
predicates.female_hindu_has_actual_possession: The female Hindu physically possesses the property.
predicates.another_person_has_only_permissive_posse: Another person holds the property with the female Hindu’s permission and has not displaced her legally recognised possession.

issues.definition: When a female Hindu has property and either physically possesses it or another person holds it only permissively, the property is treated as possessed by her for the purpose of the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A reversioner cannot maintain a suit challenging an adoption where, even on the assumption that the adoption is invalid, the widow’s possession makes her the full owner and no restricted estate is established.
material_facts: A reversioner brought a suit seeking a declaration that the widow’s adoption was invalid.
The court considered the preliminary objection on the assumption that the adoption was invalid, in which event the widow was entitled to her husband’s estate.
The alleged adopted son’s possession was permissive, leaving the widow in constructive possession.
The will’s provision for a restricted estate depended on disagreement between the widow and the trustees, and no such disagreement was shown.
The agreement concerning the adoption did not confer an estate on the widow; it provided that she would remain in possession and enjoyment of the property.
The appellant relied on a reversioner’s right to preserve a limited owner’s estate for the reversioners.
issues.conclusion: Section 14 applied, the widow became the full owner of her husband’s estate, and the reversioner’s suit was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, enlarged the widow’s interest because she constructively possessed the property. Section 14(2) did not apply: the will’s restriction was conditional on a disagreement that was not established, and the agreement did not confer a restricted estate. Under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, and illustration (f), a reversioner’s right to seek relief is directed to preserving the estate of a limited owner for the reversioners; it does not give the reversioner that right against a full owner.

rule.if: reversioner_challenge_suit and adoption_assumed_invalid and widow_entitled_to_estate and permissive_holder_possession and no_restricted_estate_established

predicates.reversioner_challenge_suit: A reversioner brings a suit seeking a declaration that a widow’s adoption is invalid.
predicates.adoption_assumed_invalid: The court considers the suit on the premise that the challenged adoption is invalid.
predicates.widow_entitled_to_estate: On that premise, the widow is entitled to her deceased husband’s estate.
predicates.permissive_holder_possession: Another person’s possession of the estate is permissive, leaving the widow in constructive possession.
predicates.no_restricted_estate_established: The evidence does not establish that the widow received only a restricted estate, including because a conditional restriction was not triggered or an agreement did not confer an estate.

issues.definition: If a reversioner challenges an adoption, the court assumes it invalid, the widow is entitled to the estate and remains in constructive possession through a permissive holder, and no restricted estate is established, the reversioner’s suit is not maintainable.
